The stated final answer, q·(q·q) + 1·q = q³ + q, cannot be correct. The trivial partition of the plane into single points already uses only q² + q + 1 arcs. For every q ≥ 2 we have q³ + q > q² + q + 1, so q³ + q is not the minimum. For q = 2 it gives 10, but PG(2,2) has only 7 points.

The final line also contradicts the boxed answer in the solution, which says q for even q and q + 1 for odd q. The reasoning in the solution has gaps as well. It asserts that the counting lower bound is achieved without proof. Its q = 4 line is also muddled: it says "k ≥ 4" because 3 × 6 < 21, which is right, but then calls that "q" without checking that the bound is attained. In any case, the final answer as written is wrong.

VERDICT: REJECT
